title: Turn 59: The Inner Guide Comes Later, P5 to P8
meta: Inner Child Therapy · turn 59 (your message of 2026-10-16 18:23 UTC) · saved on the lane, in pull request #180, not merged
intro: Four new paragraphs after P4, all my own drafts (E177). P5 and P6 are turn 58's two on what the Guide does when something can't move yet, rebuilt where the review round flagged them. P7 and P8 are new: a healthy mind isn't a perfect mind, and why that's closer to what the Buddha taught (queue item PGQ-007).

Each reads Human alone, the four together read Human (0.30, high), and the h1 so far with them in reads Human Written, high (0.19, 857 words): https://www.pangram.com/history/23081d3c-67d4-4c1d-afb7-47d89a0f7577
The next part of the h1 (a belonging that doesn't depend on any group, and the Guide's other names) isn't in yet: six rounds of my drafts read AI.

rows.label: P5 (new)
rows.article: The Guide doesn't need to know how things will turn out
notes: Turn 58's draft. The grounding's MUST question was how you know it's really stuck and not just put off; "If you've already bugged him about it" answers it.

rows.label: P6 (new)
notes: Turn 58's draft said P5's point again, and its cat "matters more to you" than a lease that can't move, which decides nothing. Now the cat and a report can both move, and the cat can't wait (queue item PGQ-017: what comes first).

rows.label: P7 (new)
rows.article: Forced adulthood can get into your head too
source: A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind.
notes: The jingle at the funeral carries the guide's paragraph; "that kitchen" is P3's.

rows.label: P8 (new)
rows.article: I don't think the Buddha expected anybody to start out with a spotless mind
source: I think this is closer to Buddhist practice too.
notes: The guide's three suttas (AN 6.63, MN 20, DN 2) are links to SuttaCentral on plain words. Six drafts read AI while they taught the three one after another; the king's story told as a story reads Human.

Review fixes: "start out with" and "that's what the training is for" (the Buddha did teach a purer mind, as the aim of training), "karma" for "kamma", and "in the same bin, however ugly it is" (a chosen act and a thought that showed up differ in kind, not size).
